headline.text: Best paper idea (sample data): Hold PEPE, short its perpetual (SmallEx), about 45% a year after costs (estimate), about $37 a month on $1,000. Risk med.

items.title: Hold WIF, short its perpetual (Bybit)
items.detail: Pays 0.0400% every 4 hours, about 87.6% a year before costs. I count 60% of it because rates fall back. Fees and slippage 0.46% of the position. Price gap to spot now +0.27%.
items.why: Everyone sees the same rate: more money piles in, the rate falls, or it turns negative and you pay instead. The profit is also eaten by fees every time you open and close.
items.warning: Your money sits on an exchange, not in your own wallet. If it freezes, is hacked or fails, you can lose all of it. A fast price spike can liquidate the short before the coin covers it.

items.title: USDe peg gap: buy below one dollar, redeem at one dollar
items.detail: USDe trades at $0.9962, a 0.38% gap to $1.00. Redeeming takes about 2 days; fee and slippage 0.15%.
items.why: Big traders close peg gaps within minutes, and redemption usually needs an account, a minimum size and KYC that a small holder does not have. If you cannot redeem you just hold the coin.
items.warning: A stablecoin that is off its peg may be falling for a real reason. In a true depeg the loss can be many times the gap. Money is locked while you wait to redeem.

items.title: Same event, two prices: Will the Fed cut rates in December 2026?
items.detail: Yes costs 60 cents on Polymarket and sells at 66 cents on Kalshi: a 6-cent gap on a 94-cent pair. Resolves in about 36 days.
items.why: These gaps are usually not free money: the two venues often word the question differently (dates, sources, tie rules), so one leg can win and the other lose. Thin books also mean the price you see is gone when you click.
items.warning: Money is locked on two venues until the event resolves. If the rules differ you can lose the whole pair. Deposits and withdrawals have their own costs and limits.

notes: Paper only. ARBITER never trades and never asks for a key. Every number is an estimate on $1,000.

Assumptions: funding positions held 30 days, 60% of today's funding rate counted, 20% margin kept beside the coin (so $1,000 of position ties up $1,200), taker fees 0.10% spot and 0.05% perp per side, slippage 0.04% per leg.
The bar to beat: a plain 4% savings rate plus a risk allowance (+1 low, +4 medium, +10 high points).
Carry that looks easy is usually paid for by a risk you cannot see in the number: exchange failure, a depeg, or two venues that mean different things.
note: EXAMPLE numbers, not real: a bundled sample shown when the live feeds cannot be reached.
